tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

from decimal import Decimal, getcontext
import itertools
getcontext().prec = 80
G = (Decimal(5).sqrt() - 1)/2
H = Decimal('0.5')
def run(choices, iters=40):
    # choices: dict iteration -> 'L' or 'R' for ties (exact symmetric configurations)
    a, b = Decimal(0), Decimal(1)
    c = b - G*(b - a); d = a + G*(b - a)
    ties = []
    for k in range(iters):
        dc, dd = abs(c - H), abs(d - H)
        if abs(dc - dd) < Decimal(10)**-60:
            ch = choices.get(k, 'R')
            ties.append(k)
            left = ch == 'L'
        else:
            left = dc < dd
        if left:
            b, d = d, c
            c = b - G*(b - a)
        else:
            a, c = c, d
            d = a + G*(b - a)
    return (a + b)/2 - H, ties
base, ties = run({})
print('ties at', ties, 'base', float(base))
targets = [1.350445e-9, 3.01969e-9, 8.4215e-9]

    okq = 0; oka = 0
    for L, T, p, q, arc1, arc2 in cases:
        cen, r0, st, t = geo((0.0, 0.0), (L, 0.0), T)
        if rv == 'c/2sin': r = r0
        elif rv == '|a-c|': r = math.sqrt(cen[0]**2 + cen[1]**2)
        elif rv == 'hypot(a-c)': r = chypot(0.0 - cen[0], 0.0 - cen[1])
        else: r = math.sqrt((L - cen[0])**2 + cen[1]**2)
        n = chords(r, t)
        if ev_form == 'r(cos,sin)':
            E = lambda a: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(a), cen[1] + r*math.sin(a))
        else:
            vx, vy = 0.0 - cen[0], 0.0 - cen[1]

        pts = [E(st + (t*k/n if dform == '(t*k)/n' else t*(k/n))) for k in range(n + 1)]
        dd, k, s = nearest_chord(p, pts)
        fc = k/n + s*((k+1)/n - k/n)
        if E(st + t*fc) == q: okq += 1
        if T*fc == arc1: oka += 1
    res.append((okq, oka, rv, stv, ev_form, dform))
res.sort(key=lambda x: -(x[0] + x[1]))
for x in res[:10]: print(x)

import math, sys, itertools
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import chypot, D2R, ulpdiff, nextf
from polarc import geo, chords, outside_cases, nearest_chord
cases = outside_cases()
G = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0.618033988749895
def golden(D, a, b):
    for _ in range(40):
        w = b - a
        c = b - G*w; d = a + G*w
        if D(c) < D(d): b = d
        else: a = c
    return (a + b)/2
stats = {}
for L, T, p, q, arc1 in cases:
    cen, r, st, t = geo((0.0, 0.0), (L, 0.0), T)
    n = chords(r, t)
    E = lambda f: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(st + t*f), cen[1] + r*math.sin(st + t*f))
    pts = [(lambda a: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(a), cen[1] + r*math.sin(a)))(st + t*k/n) for k in range(n + 1)]
    dd, k, s = nearest_chord(p, pts)
    fc = k/n + s*((k+1)/n - k/n)
    h = 1.0/(n + 1)
    D = lambda f: (lambda c: (c[0]-p[0])**2 + (c[1]-p[1])**2)(E(f))
    f = golden(D, fc - h, fc + h)
    qq = E(f)
    if chypot(qq[0]-p[0], qq[1]-p[1]) >= dd: qq = E(fc); f = fc
    # offset of p from the arc
    off = round(math.hypot(p[0]-cen[0], p[1]-cen[1]) - r, 4)
    key = (T, off)
    st_ = stats.setdefault(key, [0, 0, []])
    st_[1] += 1
    if qq == q: st_[0] += 1
    else:
        fo = arc1/T
        st_[2].append('%+.1e' % ((fo - f)/(2*h)))
for k, v in sorted(stats.items()):
    print(k, '%d/%d' % (v[0], v[1]), ' '.join(v[2]))

sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import chypot, D2R, ulpdiff, nextf
from polarc import chords, inside_cases, nearest_chord
cases = inside_cases()
def geo_b(a, b, deg, v):
    t = math.radians(deg)
    dx, dy = b[0]-a[0], b[1]-a[1]
    c = math.sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)
    m = ((a[0]+b[0])/2, (a[1]+b[1])/2)
    nrm = (-dy/c, dx/c)
    if v == 'bulge':
        be = math.tan(t/4.0)
        h = (c/2.0)*(1.0 - be*be)/(2.0*be)
        r = abs((c/2.0)*(1.0 + be*be)/(2.0*be))
        cen = (m[0] + nrm[0]*h, m[1] + nrm[1]*h)
    elif v == 'bulge2':
        be = math.tan(t/4.0)
        r = c*(1.0 + be*be)/(4.0*abs(be))
        sag = be*c/2.0
        # centre: from midpoint toward the left normal by (r - |sag|) on the side opposite the bulge
        h = (r - abs(sag))*(1.0 if be > 0 else -1.0)
        cen = (m[0] + nrm[0]*h, m[1] + nrm[1]*h)
    elif v == 'cot':
        h = (c/2.0)/math.tan(t/2.0)
        r = abs((c/2.0)/math.sin(t/2.0))
        cen = (m[0] + nrm[0]*h, m[1] + nrm[1]*h)
    else:
        r = c/(2.0*abs(math.sin(t/2.0)))
        h = r*math.cos(t/2.0)*(1.0 if t > 0 else -1.0)
        cen = (m[0] + nrm[0]*h, m[1] + nrm[1]*h)
    st = math.atan2(a[1]-cen[1], a[0]-cen[0])
    return cen, r, st, t
for v in ['trig', 'bulge', 'bulge2', 'cot']:
    for rr in ['geo', '|a-c|']:
        okq = 0; oka = 0
        for L, T, p, q, arc1, arc2 in cases:
            cen, r, st, t = geo_b((0.0, 0.0), (L, 0.0), T, v)
            if rr == '|a-c|': r = math.sqrt(cen[0]**2 + cen[1]**2)
            n = chords(r, t)
            P = lambda a: (cen[0] + r*math.cos(a), cen[1] + r*math.sin(a))
            pts = [P(st + t*k/n) for k in range(n + 1)]
            dd, k, s = nearest_chord(p, pts)
            fc = k/n + s*((k+1)/n - k/n)
            if P(st + t*fc) == q: okq += 1
            if T*fc == arc1: oka += 1
        print(okq, oka, v, rr)

import math, sys, json, pickle, itertools, io, contextlib
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    from polbase import chypot, ulpdiff, nextf
    from bspl3 import deboor_v
    from bspl import default_knots
    from refit3 import drawn
cases = pickle.load(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol50.pkl', 'rb'))
Gs = {'lit': 0.618033988749895, 'g1': (math.sqrt(5) - 1)/2}
def golden_re(D, a, b, G):
    for _ in range(40):
        w = b - a
        c = b - G*w; d = a + G*w
        if D(c) < D(d): b = d
        else: a = c
    return (a + b)/2
def golden_reuse(D, a, b, G):
    c = b - G*(b - a); d = a + G*(b - a)
    fc, fd = D(c), D(d)
    for _ in range(40):
        if fc < fd:
            b, d, fd = d, c, fc
            c = b - G*(b - a); fc = D(c)
        else:
            a, c, fc = c, d, fd
            d = a + G*(b - a); fd = D(d)
    return (a + b)/2
for gn, G in Gs.items():
    for gname, gf in [('re', golden_re), ('reuse', golden_reuse)]:
        for hv in ['range/M', 'range/(M-1)', 'range/(M+1)']:
            ok = 0; tot = 0; errs = []
            for ctrl, p, e1, e2 in cases:
                P = [list(map(float, c)) for c in ctrl]
                pp = 3; U = default_knots(len(P), pp)
                C = lambda u: deboor_v(P, U, pp, u, 'mix')
                D = drawn(P, U, pp)
                M = len(D)
                best = None
                for i in range(M - 1):
                    (ua, A), (ub, B) = D[i], D[i+1]
                    dx, dy = B[0]-A[0], B[1]-A[1]
                    s = ((p[0]-A[0])*dx + (p[1]-A[1])*dy)/(dx*dx + dy*dy)
                    s = max(0.0, min(1.0, s))
                    Q = (A[0] + s*dx, A[1] + s*dy)
                    dd = chypot(p[0]-Q[0], p[1]-Q[1])
                    if best is None or dd < best[0]: best = (dd, ua + s*(ub - ua))
                dch, uc = best
                h = 1.0/M if hv == 'range/M' else (1.0/(M - 1) if hv == 'range/(M-1)' else 1.0/(M + 1))
                Dist = lambda u: (lambda c: (c[0]-p[0])**2 + (c[1]-p[1])**2)(C(u))
                u = gf(Dist, uc - h, uc + h, G)
                qq = C(u)
                if chypot(qq[0]-p[0], qq[1]-p[1]) >= dch: u = uc
                uo = e1['knots'][-1]
                tot += 1
                if u == uo: ok += 1
                else: errs.append('%+.1e' % ((uo - u)/(2*h)))
            print(gn, gname, hv, '%d/%d' % (ok, tot), ' '.join(errs[:14]))

SPLIT = 2.0**27 + 1
def _sq(x):
    xc = x*SPLIT
    xh = x - xc + xc
    xl = x - xh
    hi = x*x
    lo = xh*xh - hi + 2*xh*xl + xl*xl
    return hi, lo
def hypot(x, y):
    x = abs(x); y = abs(y)
    bx = struct.unpack('<Q', struct.pack('<d', x))[0]
    by = struct.unpack('<Q', struct.pack('<d', y))[0]
    if bx < by:
        x, y = y, x; bx, by = by, bx
    ex = bx >> 52; ey = by >> 52
    if ey == 0x7ff: return y

    if ex - ey > 64: return x + y
    z = 1.0
    if ex > 0x3ff + 510:
        z = 2.0**700; x *= 2.0**-700; y *= 2.0**-700
    elif ey < 0x3ff - 450:
        z = 2.0**-700; x *= 2.0**700; y *= 2.0**700
    hx, lx = _sq(x)

import math, sys, json, pickle
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
from polbase import nextf, ulpdiff, chypot
from polpl import Poly
cases = pickle.load(open('/tmp/views-lines/pol65.pkl', 'rb'))
def split_point(e1):
    if 'end' in e1: return tuple(e1['end'])
    return tuple(e1['points'][-1])
def arcs_of(e):
    if 'arc' in e: return [e['arc']]
    return e.get('arcs', [])
for pts, arcs, i, fr, off, p, e1, e2 in cases:
    P = Poly(pts, arcs)
    u, q, pol = P.nearest(p, 'a')
    qo = split_point(e1)
    seg = min(int(math.floor(u)), len(P.segs) - 1)
    f = u - seg
    T = arcs[seg]
    a1o = arcs_of(e1)[-1]
    a2o = arcs_of(e2)[0]
    fo = a1o/T
    print('arcs', arcs, 'seg', seg, 'fr', fr, 'off', off, 'q', 'same' if q == qo else 'diff', ' T*f==a1o', T*f == a1o, ' ulps(fo-f) %d' % ulpdiff(fo, f), ' T*(1-f)==a2o', T*(1 - f) == a2o)

    f0 = a1/T

        found['a2=T(1-f)'] = True

    for k in ['a2=T(1-f)', 'a1=Tf', 'a1=T-a2']:
        cnt[(k, found.get(k, False))] += 1
print(sorted(cnt.items()))

import math, sys, io, contextlib
sys.path.insert(0, '/tmp/views-lines')
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(io.StringIO()):
    from bspl3 import deboor_v
from fractions import Fraction as Fr
# exact natural cubic interpolation through (0,0),(1000,500),(2000,0) at params s; returns control points
def solve_exact(s, pts):
    # unknowns: 5 control points; equations: interpolation at s0,s1,s2 + second derivative 0 at both ends
    import itertools
    kn = [s[0]]*4 + [s[1]] + [s[2]]*4
    def basis(u, i, p, k):
        # Cox-de Boor exact
        if p == 0:
            if kn[i] <= u < kn[i+1] or (u == kn[-1] and kn[i] < u <= kn[i+1]): return Fr(1)
            return Fr(0)
        a = Fr(0)
        if kn[i+p] != kn[i]: a += (u - kn[i])/(kn[i+p] - kn[i])*basis(u, i, p-1, k)
        if kn[i+p+1] != kn[i+1]: a += (kn[i+p+1] - u)/(kn[i+p+1] - kn[i+1])*basis(u, i+1, p-1, k)
        return a
    n = 5
    rows = []
    for j in range(3):
        rows.append([basis(Fr(s[j]), i, 3, 0) for i in range(n)])
    # second derivative at ends for clamped cubic: P0..P2 at start: 6/(d1 d2) etc; use finite formula
    d = s[1] - s[0]
    # for knots [0,0,0,0,a,b,b,b,b]: C''(0) = 6/(a*a)... derive numerically via exact second difference of basis? simpler: use known formula
    # C''(0) = 6/(t4-t1) * [ (P2-P1)/(t5-t2) - (P1-P0)/(t4-t1) ] for p=3 with t1=t2=t3=0
    t = kn
    r0 = [Fr(0)]*n
    A = Fr(6)/(t[4]-t[1]); B1 = Fr(1)/(t[5]-t[2]); B0 = Fr(1)/(t[4]-t[1])
    r0[0] = A*B0; r0[1] = -A*(B0 + B1); r0[2] = A*B1
    rn = [Fr(0)]*n
    # end: symmetric
    A = Fr(6)/(t[7]-t[4]); C1 = Fr(1)/(t[7]-t[4]); C0 = Fr(1)/(t[6]-t[3])
    rn[4] = A*C1; rn[3] = -A*(C1 + C0); rn[2] = A*C0
    M = rows + [r0, rn]
    rhs = [Fr(p) for p in pts] + [Fr(0), Fr(0)]
    # gaussian exact
    m = len(M)
    Aug = [M[i] + [rhs[i]] for i in range(m)]
    for c in range(m):
        piv = next(r for r in range(c, m) if Aug[r][c] != 0)
        Aug[c], Aug[piv] = Aug[piv], Aug[c]
        for r in range(m):
            if r != c and Aug[r][c] != 0:
                f = Aug[r][c]/Aug[c][c]

def norm_turn(t, turn):

def run(a, b, deg, d, line_y, want):
    cen, r, st, t = seg_geo(a, b, deg)
    rr = r - d if t > 0 else r + d
    k = rr/r
    A = (cen[0] + (a[0]-cen[0])*k, cen[1] + (a[1]-cen[1])*k)
    B = (cen[0] + (b[0]-cen[0])*k, cen[1] + (b[1]-cen[1])*k)
    # intersection of y = line_y with circle (cen, rr): foot-based as my meet
    # line through (0, line_y) and (1000, line_y)
    p0 = (0.0, line_y); p1 = (1000.0, line_y)
    dx, dy = p1[0]-p0[0], p1[1]-p0[1]
    l2 = dx*dx + dy*dy
    s = ((cen[0]-p0[0])*dx + (cen[1]-p0[1])*dy)/l2
    fx, fy = p0[0] + s*dx, p0[1] + s*dy
    h2 = rr*rr - ((fx-cen[0])**2 + (fy-cen[1])**2)
    hh = math.sqrt(h2)/math.sqrt(l2)
    cands = [(fx - dx*hh, fy - dy*hh), (fx + dx*hh, fy + dy*hh)]
    target = ((1000.0 + A[0])/2, (line_y + A[1])/2)
    c = min(cands, key=lambda q: math.hypot(q[0]-target[0], q[1]-target[1]))
    out = {}

    a0 = math.atan2(c[1]-cen[1], c[0]-cen[0]); a1 = math.atan2(B[1]-cen[1], B[0]-cen[0])

    cen2, r2_, st2, t2 = seg_geo(A, B, deg)
    a0 = math.atan2(c[1]-cen2[1], c[0]-cen2[0]); a1 = math.atan2(B[1]-cen2[1], B[0]-cen2[0])
    out['moved centre'] = math.degrees(norm_turn(a1 - a0, t))
    # (3) deg - trimmed part
    sa = math.atan2(A[1]-cen[1], A[0]-cen[0])
    cut = norm_turn(a0 - sa, t)
    out['T - deg(cut)'] = deg - math.degrees(norm_turn(math.atan2(c[1]-cen[1], c[0]-cen[0]) - math.atan2(A[1]-cen[1], A[0]-cen[0]), t))

    f = norm_turn(math.atan2(c[1]-cen[1], c[0]-cen[0]) - st, t)/t
    out['T*(1-f)'] = deg*(1 - f)

]

    p0 = (xline, -1000.0); p1 = (xline, 1000.0)
    dx, dy = p1[0]-p0[0], p1[1]-p0[1]
    l2 = dx*dx + dy*dy
    s = ((cen[0]-p0[0])*dx + (cen[1]-p0[1])*dy)/l2
    fx, fy = p0[0] + s*dx, p0[1] + s*dy

            (ua, A), (ub, B) = pts[i], pts[i+1]
            dx, dy = B[0]-A[0], B[1]-A[1]
            s_ = ((p[0]-A[0])*dx + (p[1]-A[1])*dy)/(dx*dx + dy*dy)
            s_ = max(0.0, min(1.0, s_))
            Q = (A[0] + s_*dx, A[1] + s_*dy)
            dd = chypot(p[0]-Q[0], p[1]-Q[1])
            if best is None or dd < best[0]: best = (dd, ua + s_*(ub - ua))
        dch, uc = best
        hh = scale/(n + 1)
        lo, hi = max(uc - hh, 0.0) if scale > 0 else min(uc - hh, 0.0), min(uc + hh, scale) if scale > 0 else max(uc + hh, scale)
        a, b = (lo, hi) if lo < hi else (hi, lo)
        Df = lambda u: (lambda c: chypot(c[0]-p[0], c[1]-p[1]))(E(u))
        for _ in range(40):
            w = b - a
            c = b - G*w; d = a + G*w
            if Df(c) < Df(d): b = d
            else: a = c
        u = (a + b)/2
        q = E(u)
        if chypot(q[0]-p[0], q[1]-p[1]) >= dch: u = uc
        if dom == 'f': a1 = T*u
        elif dom == 'deg': a1 = u
        else: a1 = math.degrees(u)
        out.append('%s:%s' % (dom, 'OK' if a1 == a1o else '%+d' % ulpdiff(a1, a1o)))
    print(T, p, ' '.join(out))

content.text:
I've committed everything on branch `worktree-agent-a3aa4b1d689cb6d8a`; the last commit is `f08c785` and the working tree is clean. The local suite now gives 1114/1173 identical to the original. The remaining differences are about two-thirds other agents' commands (split, duplicate_view, sheet, elevation, inspect, the dimension check). The rest are last-digit differences in my offset, trim and refit output, listed below.

**What changed since the last report**
- **Nearest point on a curve.** I found the original's method and reimplemented it. It finds the nearest chord, then runs 40 golden-section steps in the curve's own parameter. The search bracket is the parameter range divided by the number of drawn points on each side, clipped to the range. The refined point is used only if it is nearer than the chord. A polyline's parameter is segment index plus fraction (this is why the original splits [1000,300] to `300.00000000000006`). Circles and ellipses run in degrees, splines on their knots.
  - Against the original's full-precision split output: circles 65/65, ellipses 18/18, control splines 154/154. Polyline arcs are 124/192 for single arcs and 49/72 for polylines; the rest differ in the last few bits of a point or turn.
- **Splitting.** Arc halves now turn `arc·f` and `arc·(1−f)`, which matched 192/192. A spline through points is split by refitting each half (256 samples, unrounded points, the tangent kept where it is cut).
- **Arc centre.** It is now computed as half the chord over tan(half the turn). That raised exact matches on inside points from 75 to 95 of 128.
- **Ellipses** are drawn and evaluated by their parameter in degrees, as their span is stored.
- **trim_extend.** The end-moved arc turn is now the crossing's angle in degrees.
- **trim_extend undo.** It now records its own undo step even when no line changes, as the original does.

**Per command**
- **`detail_line`, `join_polyline`, `explode`:** match in every test of mine. The only differences are cases that use another agent's command (`inspect`, `duplicate_view`, or the dimension check).
- **`vertex`:** every test matches, including points off the convex side of arcs (e.g. `15.000000027`), spline knots at full precision, fitted splines and closed polylines. On new cases it went from 12/15 to 15/15.
- **`convert_spline`:** spline-through-points → control points matches. Control points → spline through points matches when the refit is short. Long refits drift apart (cs2 2/9, cs3 5/7, cs4 4/10, cs1 28/29) because the selection of new points cascades from tiny differences.
  - The cause is that the original evaluates splines through points differently from my B-spline, in the last bits. I couldn't pin down its formula; it is not exact rational evaluation, Hermite, Bernstein or de Boor with several solver variants.
- **`offset`:** lines and arcs match except a 1–2 ulp difference in a trimmed offset arc's turn (4 cases). Offsets of ellipses and splines pick different points for the same reason as above (4 cases).
- **`trim_extend`:** lines match. For arcs, the start-moved turn and some crossings differ by a few ulps. When both ends are exactly equally near the keep point, the original sometimes extends the other end (2 cases). te5 is 20/26 and te2 is 42/44.
  - The new end-moved formula traded two te2 extension cases for two te5 trim cases. A 26-case survey slightly favoured it, but neither formula matches most cases, because the crossing point itself differs in the last bits.

**API changes others will see (in `src/views/curves.rs`)**
- `Near` has a new field `param`: the curve's own parameter (polyline segment index plus fraction, degrees for circles and ellipses, knots for splines).
- New: `Curve::cut_near(&Near)` (used by `split_at`), `refit_with(.., round)`, and the constants `GOLDEN` and `NARROWINGS`.
- `refine_through` and `Bspline::polish` were removed.
- EDIT's `split` for detail lines should call `lineedit::split_line`, which is now much closer to the original.

**Still needed outside my files (unchanged from my last report)**
- **Core:** substitute library GUIDs with names in all parameters.
- **Loader:** call `lines::normalize` when a file is opened, and check the model on open.
- **Shared helpers:** `model::resolve_level` and `common::find_view` differ from the original (a GUID that isn't found should give the name error; a numeric string that isn't an element should say "is not a view").
- **DIMS:** its check should refuse dimensions on joined polylines.
- **EDIT:** move, rotate and mirror should use `Curve::map`/`moved`/`turned`/`mirrored`.
- **Views:** deleting a view should delete its lines.

Scratch scripts and probes are in `/tmp/views-lines/` (outside the repo).
